result.rationale: In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff replaces `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` with `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`, and parseRefreshTokenResponse returns `refreshTokenResponse` — a safeParse wrapper ({success, data}). This wrapper is then stored directly via `data: { key }`, whereas before the parsed data was stored. So credential.key becomes the wrapper object and subsequent reads of key.access_token/expiry_date return undefined. Verified from the diff.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse wrapper object ({success, data}), and this call site stores that wrapper directly as the credential key (`data: { key }`), whereas the replaced code `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` stored the parsed data itself. On the first Google token refresh of any deployment (sync mode or not), credential.key is overwritten with {success:true,data:{...}}; every later read of credential.key.access_token/expiry_date returns undefined, so Google Calendar API calls fail authorization and the calendar stays broken until the user manually reconnects the app.
